issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer relies on handler iteration order to locate the OTLP LoggingHandler; precondition undocumented and unverified
issues.detail: The replay path scans logging.getLogger().handlers for the first LoggingHandler instance. There is no stated precondition that _setup_cloud_tracer has installed exactly one such handler, nor a postcondition if none is found (silent no-op, crash logs lost). State the invariant or assert it; silent failure of an upload path is precisely the bug this PR claims to fix. TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: Buffer has no bound; an unbounded list of LogRecord smuggled across an unknown lifetime is a memory hazard
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler.buffer is an unbounded list[LogRecord] retained from _on_setup until init_recording or _on_cleanup. If the job hangs before either, the buffer grows without limit. No termination function bounds its size. State the upper bound or enforce one; do not leave it to hope. DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE absent entirely.

issues.description: _on_cleanup re-enters init_recording with traces=False, logs=True; interaction with prior recording state is unreasoned
issues.detail: The cleanup path conditions on `_early_log_handler is not None and not _recording_initialized`, then calls init_recording. But init_recording itself stops buffering if _recording_initialized is already true or url not cloud — a redundancy that suggests the author did not state the precondition. What if init_recording was attempted and failed earlier setting _recording_initialized=True with no OTLP handler installed? Unreasoned branch.

issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry now removes every LoggingHandler from the root logger as a side effect
issues.detail: The fix removes all instances of opentelemetry's LoggingHandler from root before force_flush. The frame (what may change) was previously narrow; it now mutates global logging state for any handler subclass matching that type, including ones the user installed. State the frame explicitly or scope removal to the handler this module installed. SMUGGLED-GOTO via global side effect.

issues.description: Forcing _shutdown_fut to resolve on crash conflates two distinct postconditions under one future
issues.detail: _on_entry_done now sets _shutdown_fut with reason='job crashed' to unblock cleanup. Downstream consumers of shutdown_info previously could assume orderly shutdown semantics; now the same channel carries crash signaling. Either define the postcondition of _shutdown_fut to include crash, or use a separate signal. Overloading a future's meaning is precisely the kind of smuggled control flow that defeats reasoning.

issues.description: Unrelated changes (makefile -n auto removal, test_plugin_google_stt removal, worker.py reorder) bundled without justification
issues.detail: Removing pytest-xdist parallelism and excluding test_plugin_google_stt.py from CI is not motivated by the PR description. The worker.py reorder of _pending_assignments registration before _queue_msg is a real race fix but is undocumented in the description. A reviewer cannot reason about a change whose specification is silent. Split or annotate.

review.summary: The PR addresses a real defect — crash logs lost when sessions fail to start — but the fix accretes complexity in the logging subsystem without stating the preconditions and frames it touches. The buffered-handler scheme has no bound, locates its OTLP sink by handler-type scan rather than by stated invariant, and silently no-ops if the scan fails. _shutdown_fut is overloaded to carry crash signaling. The diff also bundles unrelated changes (pytest parallelism, a test removal, a worker.py race fix) with no specification. TESTED-NOT-PROVED on the replay path; the very behavior under repair is the one most likely to fail silently again.
